nodes.label: Defamation, Privacy and Confidence
nodes.summary: Defamation (libel and slander), defences such as justification, fair comment, privilege, the emerging HK privacy tort, and breach of confidence.

nodes.label: Defamation Overview
nodes.summary: Defamation protects reputation against false statements. Libel (permanent form, actionable per se) and slander (transient form, proof of special damage generally required). HK defamation law derived from English common law.

nodes.label: Elements of Defamation
nodes.summary: Claimant must prove: (1) a defamatory statement (tending to lower reputation), (2) referring to the claimant, (3) published to a third party. No proof of falsity initially required (rebuttable presumption).

nodes.label: Libel vs Slander
nodes.summary: Libel is defamation in permanent form (writing, broadcast, image) — actionable per se. Slander is defamation in transient form (speech, gesture) — generally requires proof of special damage unless in an excepted category.

nodes.label: Justification (Truth)
nodes.summary: The defence of justification: if the defendant proves that the statement is substantially true, the claim fails. Truth is an absolute defence in civil defamation.

nodes.label: Fair Comment / Honest Opinion
nodes.summary: Defence of fair comment (or honest opinion) protects statements of opinion on matters of public interest, based on true facts, that a fair-minded person could honestly hold. HK position needs verification.

nodes.label: Absolute Privilege
nodes.summary: Statements made in parliamentary proceedings, judicial proceedings, and certain official communications are protected by absolute privilege, regardless of malice or falsity.

nodes.label: Qualified Privilege
nodes.summary: A person may publish defamatory material without liability if they have a legal, moral or social duty to communicate it and the recipient has a corresponding interest. Defeated by malice.

nodes.label: Reynolds Defence / Public Interest
nodes.summary: Responsible journalism on matters of public interest may attract qualified privilege (Reynolds defence). Factors include seriousness of allegation, source, verification steps, and urgency. HK position requires verification.

nodes.label: Offer of Amends
nodes.summary: A statutory defence and mechanism under the Defamation Ordinance for a publisher to make an offer of amends (apology, correction, damages) to mitigate or avoid liability.

nodes.label: Internet Publishers and ISPs
nodes.summary: Liability of internet intermediaries and website operators for defamatory content posted by users. HK position on s.5 of Defamation Ordinance (innocent dissemination), notice-and-takedown, and ISP liability requires verification.

nodes.label: Privacy Tort (Emerging)
nodes.summary: HK does not have a comprehensive privacy tort. Claims for invasion of privacy may potentially be brought under the tort of intrusion upon seclusion, misuse of private information, or via the HK Bill of Rights. Requires further development.

nodes.label: Misuse of Private Information
nodes.summary: Developed from breach of confidence; protects against disclosure of private information where the claimant has a reasonable expectation of privacy. HK position requires verification. UK approach: balancing Article 8 vs Article 10 rights.

nodes.label: Breach of Confidence
nodes.summary: Equitable action protecting confidential information. Requires: (1) the information has the necessary quality of confidence, (2) it was imparted in circumstances of confidence, (3) unauthorised use causing detriment.

nodes.label: Defamation Remedies
nodes.summary: Damages (compensatory, aggravated, exemplary), injunctions, declarations, and offer of amends. Jury trial is available in HK for defamation. Damages aim to vindicate reputation and compensate for hurt feelings.

nodes.label: Defamation Ordinance (Cap. 21)
nodes.summary: HK statute governing defamation law, including defences of justification, fair comment, privilege, offer of amends, and provisions on libel and slander.

nodes.label: East Week Weekly v Secretary for Justice [2004] HKCA 123
nodes.summary: Seed case for HK defamation / privacy / freedom of speech balance. Needs paragraph verification.

nodes.label: Cheung Yu Shing v Apple Daily Ltd [2015] HKCFI 345
nodes.summary: Seed case for defamation / fair comment in HK context. Needs paragraph verification.

nodes.label: Verify Defamation Ordinance Provisions
nodes.summary: Confirm current Defamation Ordinance (Cap. 21) provisions on defences, offer of amends, ISPs, and jury trial availability.
